title: fix(codex): reap orphaned app-servers before reconnect

commit.messageHeadline: fix(codex): reap orphaned app-servers before reconnect
style(codex): avoid returning the containment timer handle
fix(codex): inspect Linux children without requiring procps
fix(codex): tolerate processes exiting during procfs reads
test(codex): normalize socket fixture binary frames
fix(codex): preserve startup errors during process registration

No source-level defect was confirmed, but this reviewer could not perform the repository-required direct sibling Codex source check. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `b8ec3a6f63d046b68df56c6f7c70473947cb0e84` **Owner decision:** Required. See [Decision needed](#decision-needed). ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | The patch is coherent and behavior-tested at its owner boundary, but the required direct upstream Codex contract check prevents a merge-ready Codex verdict in this environment. | | **Proof confidence** | 🌊 off-meta tidepool | Not applicable: This maintainer-authored PR is exempt from the external-contributor proof gate. Its body describes native crash/reconnect probes and the checked source contains a behavior-level process test, but this reviewer did not independently execute them and could not complete the required sibling Codex contract check. | | **Patch quality** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Not applicable | Not applicable: This maintainer-authored PR is exempt from the external-contributor proof gate. Its body describes native crash/reconnect probes and the checked source contains a behavior-level process test, but this reviewer did not independently execute them and could not complete the required sibling Codex contract check. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 8 items | Current main lacks this recovery path: Current main still returns the spawned stdio child directly; it has neither pre-spawn registration cleanup nor durable process registration, so the central behavior remains necessary.
Introduced owner boundary: The PR places recovery before spawn and persists the parent/child identity after spawn but before the caller can initialize the app-server.
Caller and lifecycle deadline: Shared-client startup awaits the new async start under its existing acquisition deadline and disposes a client that resolves after ownership has been released. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together The Codex plugin launches an app-server subprocess for native work. The new startup path reads prior process registrations, removes a verified orphan when its Gateway parent is gone, then persists the replacement process identity before Codex initialization. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Gateway requests Codex work] --> B[Codex stdio startup] B --> C[Process registration store] C --> D[Inspect prior Gateway owner] D -->|dead and identity verified| E[Reap orphan process tree] D -->|live or uncertain| F[Skip or fail visibly] E --> G[Spawn and register app-server] G --> H[Codex initialize and native work] ``` ## Decision needed | Question | Recommendation | |---|---| | Should this maintainer-owned POSIX recovery design proceed after a reviewer with the required sibling Codex checkout verifies the initialization and shutdown assumptions that bound orphan cleanup? | **Complete upstream contract check:** Have a Codex-area reviewer inspect the pinned app-server initialization and EOF/shutdown behavior, then resume normal merge review. | Why: The PR directly launches and drives the Codex app-server, and repository policy requires direct sibling-source inspection before a Codex verdict or proof-sufficient claim; that checkout is unavailable here. ## Before merge - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The new fail-closed recovery path can prevent Codex stdio startup when process inspection or bounded cleanup is unavailable; that is intentional, but requires maintainer acceptance for existing POSIX deployments. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The repository-required direct inspection of the Codex app-server protocol/runtime could not be completed because ../codex is absent in this review environment. - [ ] **Complete next step (P1)** - A Codex-area maintainer must complete the direct upstream contract check and accept the intentional fail-closed startup behavior before merge.

Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge. ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Verify the upstream lifecycle contract (recommended)** Before merge, record direct Codex-source confirmation that initialization prevents native work until the durable registration point and that shutdown behavior matches the recovery assumptions. 2. **Accept the fail-closed recovery tradeoff** Merge with explicit maintainer acceptance that inaccessible process inspection blocks a fresh POSIX Codex stdio connection rather than risking overlap. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Retain the owner-plugin registration design if a Codex-area maintainer confirms the direct upstream initialization and shutdown contract, then merge only after the normal exact-head CI gates are green. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes, source-reproducible with high confidence: current main starts a detached POSIX stdio child without a durable registration or reconnect-time reaper, and the added crash test encodes the hard-kill/reconnect sequence. This reviewer did not execute that sequence. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Unclear: the repair is located at the spawn owner and reuses the existing containment owner, which is the right architectural boundary, but the required direct Codex runtime-contract inspection remains unavailable.
